83	  | call_depth | procedure calls in progress |
84	  | frames_made, calls, name_uses, name_evaluations | totals over the run |
85	  | name_first_evaluations, name_repeat_evaluations | evaluations of an actual parameter for the first time, and again, for the same parameter of the same call |
86	
87	  Temporary values are not measured: the tree-walking interpreter holds
88	  them on its own call stack, which cannot be counted without changing how
89	  it runs. call_depth is the nearest measure.
90	
91	  The instrumented commit's stdout, stderr and exit code were identical to
92	  the baseline's on all 100 programs in the repository, in both dialects,
93	  with measurement on and off (200 runs, checked for `2589d00` and again
94	  for `151cdff`). That is observational equivalence over that corpus.
95	- **Repeated work:** `name_repeat_evaluations`. Call by name evaluates an
96	  actual parameter again at every use, and each actual parameter keeps its
97	  own count, so a repeat is told apart from a first evaluation. Jensen's
98	  device makes 8 procedure calls and 392 name evaluations: 16 first, 376
99	  repeats. A repeat is not always wasted work. Jensen's device relies on
100	  it, since the parameter's value changes between evaluations.
101	- **Alternative:** as Python: whatever structure the program keeps, named.
102	- **x1sim: behaviour only.** The simulator (Vakulenko's, commit
103	  `938fa03`) counts the X1 instructions it executes, but it reports the
104	  count only in a progress message every five seconds, not at the end of a
105	  run, so reading it would mean changing the simulator. And the count would
106	  not measure the X1's work. The run-time routines that the object code
107	  calls (procedure entry, `for` statements, real arithmetic, input and
108	  output) do not survive, and the simulator carries them out as 105
109	  operations written in C++, each counted as one instruction however much
110	  it does. x1sim is therefore run in behaviour mode only, for its
111	  outcomes. No step, store or cost figure is taken from it.
112	
113	## The same computation
114	
115	A program may read each stage with `ininteger` or `insymbol` as it
116	arrives, which counts as the same computation. Otherwise each stage is
117	posed by rerunning with stages 1 to k.
118

1	# Harnesses: the common contract
2	
3	*Phase 4 (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Phases"), wave 1, written against `spec-1.0`.
4	This is the part every per-system harness shares. It changes no frozen
5	file. Where the specification could not be implemented as written, or was
6	ambiguous, the reading taken here is in [`QUESTIONS.md`](QUESTIONS.md).*
7	
8	| file | what it is |
9	|---|---|
10	| `README.md` | this contract: what every per-system harness implements, and what every program is written against |
11	| [`stages.json`](stages.json) | the structure of every problem: sub-problems, instances (sizes, orders, answer modes), and per stage its number, description, queries and caps, commit and spawn, and the problem file's line. **No constants, no valid outcomes** |
12	| [`record.schema.json`](record.schema.json) | the JSON Schema of a raw record, the same for every system |
13	| [`validate.py`](validate.py) | checks raw records against the schema and the rules below (Python 3, standard library only) |
14	| [`QUESTIONS.md`](QUESTIONS.md) | what the specification leaves open, and the reading implemented |
15	| [`examples/`](examples) | **made-up** records and a made-up stages file, written by hand to test `validate.py`. Not runs, not results |
16	| `<system>/` | one per system, written by that system's harness author: `run`, `check`, its `README.md`, `S-mechanisms.md`, `qualification/` |
17	
18	Words in this file: *must*, *never* and *only* are requirements; a
19	per-system harness that cannot meet one says so in its own `QUESTIONS.md`
20	and README.
21	
22	## 1. The first principle
23	
24	**A harness observes what the system computes. It never supplies it.**
25	
26	A harness passes stages in, collects answers through the system's
27	standard mechanism for answers, reads state for `observe()`, enforces the
28	budget and the safety limit, and writes the record. It does not, on the
29	system's or the program's behalf:
30	
31	- suspend a computation, or wait for information;
32	- search, backtrack, or enumerate values;
33	- schedule, interleave or arbitrate between computations, or run
34	  computations concurrently itself (`PROTOCOL.md`: concurrency is a
35	  mechanism of the configuration);
36	- propagate constraints, or simplify, reconstruct, complete or combine
37	  answers;
38	- combine stages, work out the net information of a reposed run, or skip
39	  a replayed stage;
40	- order, choose, retry or re-pose goals on its own.
41	
42	Where a configuration lacks a mechanism, the harness does not make up for
43	it. The program must, as S code counted against that configuration, or
44	the problem is *not expressible* there. Everything a harness does beyond
45	passing stages in, collecting answers and reading state is listed in its
46	README as a possible confound, and copied into each record's
47	`run.confounds`.
48	
49	## 2. Terms
50	
51	| term | meaning |
52	|---|---|
53	| **instance** | one thing a harness runs: a sub-problem at one size, in one arrival or spawn order, in one answer mode. Its id comes from `stages.json` (`P01a`, `P02b.R2R1R3`, `P12c.n16.any`, `P13d.n10000`, `P16a.n1000.interleaved`). A sub-problem with one instance has the sub-problem's own id |
54	| **run** | one invocation of `harnesses/<system>/run`: one configuration, one instance, one mode, every stage of the instance in order. It writes one raw record |
55	| **stage** | as the problem file numbers it (`stages.json` gives the line). Stage k's information is held by the program, never by the harness |
56	| **computation** | `main`, the instance's one computation (or its top level); or a computation started with `spawn()` (P09a, P09b, P16b), named as `stages.json` names it |
57	| **attempt** | one try at a stage under the safety limit. A stage has one attempt, or two when the first was stopped by the safety limit and the problem allows a rerun |
58	| **query** | one call of `answers(cap)` on one computation at the end of a stage. Each stage of `stages.json` lists its queries with their caps |
59	
60	The query of a stage is always about all the information of stages 1 to k
61	(`SPECIFICATION.md`, "Stages and monotonicity"), over the sub-problem's
62	unknowns. `stages.json` lists those unknowns by name; their values are
63	for the classifiers.
64	
65	## 3. How a run is driven
66	
67	    harnesses/<system>/run CONFIGURATION PROBLEM SUBPROBLEM MODE PROGRAM OUTDIR
68	
69	| argument | value |
70	|---|---|
71	| CONFIGURATION | a configuration of `systems/<system>/README.md`, by its name there (`absys-depth-first`, `plain`, `core`, `x1sim`, ...) |
72	| PROBLEM | `P01` … `P16` |
73	| SUBPROBLEM | an **instance id** from `stages.json`, which for a sub-problem with one instance is the sub-problem id (`P07c`), and otherwise names its parameters (`P12a.n8.all`). See `QUESTIONS.md`, Q2 |
74	| MODE | `behaviour`, `cost` or `storage` (section 8) |
75	| PROGRAM | the program's path, relative to the repository root |
76	| OUTDIR | where the raw record is written: `results/<system>/<configuration>/<problem>/raw/` (section 10) |
77	
78	Exit status: **0** when a valid record was written, whatever the run's
79	outcome (an *error*, *budget* or *timeout* stage is a result, not a
80	failure of the harness); **2** for a usage error (unknown configuration,
81	instance or mode; a mode the systems file does not allow for that
82	configuration, such as `cost` for *x1sim*), with no record written;
83	**3** when the harness itself failed and could not write a valid record.
84	A harness fault that still allows a record is written into
85	`harness_faults` and exits 0.
86	
87	**The harness runs inside that system's pinned Linux image**
88	(`sandbox/README.md`, `PINS.md`): `cp-systems:spec-1.0` (Absys, ALGOL 60,
89	x1sim), the pinned `swipl:11.0.1` image, the pinned `python:3.13.7`
90	image. It assumes nothing of the host. It needs only what the image has,
91	plus the repository mounted at a path it is given or finds from its own
92	location. It records the system build it ran (section 9). The launcher
93	outside the container (whatever starts it) is not part of the harness and
94	may not change what it does; it may pass the image digest in, by an
95	environment variable the system harness names, since the harness cannot
96	always read it from inside.
97	
98	What `run` does, in this order, and nothing else:
99	
100	1. Read `harnesses/stages.json`; find the instance; take its stages, its
101	   queries and caps, its commit and spawn stages, and its limits (a
102	   problem's `limits`, else `default_limits`).
103	2. Check the program with nothing but reading its bytes (SHA-256) and,
104	   where the systems file needs it, the constants input (section 11).
105	3. For k = 1 … K: **pose** stage k (section 4); for each spawned
106	   computation of the stage, **spawn** it; for each query of the stage,
107	   **answers(cap)**; then **observe()** and **print()**; then record the
108	   attempt. Apply the safety limit (section 7); after a stop, rerun once
109	   where allowed.
110	4. Write the record, then validate it with `validate.py`. A record that
111	   does not validate is a harness fault (exit 3), kept beside the output
112	   under the name `<run_id>.INVALID.json`, never silently dropped.
113	
114	`run` never decides, from what a stage returned, to pose a different
115	stage, to skip one, or to stop early. The only things that change how the
116	next stage is posed are the ones `PROTOCOL.md` names: *budget*, *error*,
117	and (`QUESTIONS.md`, Q7) *timeout*. P13's rule that larger n are not run
118	after a limit stop is applied by whoever runs the batch, across runs, not
119	by `run` (Q10).
120	
121	## 4. The operations
122	
123	These are `PROTOCOL.md`'s, made concrete. A per-system harness implements
124	exactly these and nothing that orders, chooses or re-poses goals on its
125	own.
126	
127	### pose(stage)
128	
129	Gives the system the information of stage k, in one of two ways, chosen
130	by the configuration's systems file ("The same computation"), never by
131	the harness from results:
132	
133	- **incremental**: stage k is received into the computation that holds
134	  stages 1 to k−1 (an Absys session, a SWI-Prolog *session* engine, a
135	  Python or ALGOL 60 program that reads each stage from its input as it
136	  arrives). Recorded `posed.how = "incremental"`.
137	- **reposed**: a new computation is started, and stages 1 to k are
138	  replayed into it **in order, every one of them, replacements and
139	  withdrawals included** (P10, P15d). The program carries them out. The
140	  harness never works out the net information itself, never drops a
141	  stage that a later one replaced or withdrew, and never merges stages.
142	  Recorded `posed.how = "reposed"`, `posed.replayed = [1, …, k−1]`.
143	
144	Stage 1 is always `fresh`. What the harness gives the program is only:
145	which stage to pose (k), for a reposed run the list of stages to replay
146	(1 … k−1) and any replayed commitments (below), and the instance's
147	parameters (n, order, answer mode, as `stages.json` gives them). The
148	program holds the stage information. The harness never passes a constant
149	of a problem.
150	
151	**No anticipation** (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Writing a program", rule 5): the
152	harness tells the program about stage k only when stage k is posed, and
153	never tells it how many stages follow.
154	
155	### spawn(computation)
156	
157	P09a, P09b and P16b. Starts a separate computation **in the same
158	instance of the system**, sharing one database, never in a separate
159	operating system process (`PROTOCOL.md`). `stages.json` lists the
160	computations a stage spawns (`spawns`) and, for P09a, the order
161	(`spawn_order`).
162	
163	- Where the configuration can run computations side by side, `spawn`
164	  returns at once (`side_by_side: true`).
165	- Where it cannot, the first runs to its end or its budget, and then the
166	  next (`side_by_side: false`).
167	- Each spawned computation has its own budget and its own execution
168	  state, recorded separately.
169	- P16b only: where the configuration does not allow separate
170	  computations to share unknowns, the four contributions are posed as one
171	  conjunction in `main` (`spawn_fallback`), with `fallback_queries`, and
172	  that is recorded. Which configurations allow it is the systems file's
173	  and the system harness's statement, not the harness's judgement on a
174	  run.
175	
176	The harness may use the configuration's own mechanism for starting a
177	computation (an engine, a thread, a program's own spawn), as the program
178	asks for it. It may not interleave computations itself.
179	
180	### answers(cap)
181	
182	Collects the answers the system reports, **through its standard mechanism
183	for enumerating them** (each systems file says what it is; for Python and
184	ALGOL 60 it is the values the program prints), until the mechanism is
185	exhausted, the budget runs out, or `cap` answers have been collected.
186	`cap` is 1 for an *any one* query and 20 otherwise, as `stages.json`
187	gives it per query. The harness never asks for an answer the mechanism
188	did not offer, never filters or deduplicates answers, and never stops
189	early because the answers look complete. Each answer is recorded
190	**verbatim**, as the mechanism produced it, with `ended_by`:
191	
192	| ended_by | when |
193	|---|---|
194	| `exhausted` | the mechanism reported no more answers |
195	| `cap` | `cap` answers were collected; the mechanism was not asked again |
196	| `budget` | the budget ran out while collecting |
197	| `timeout` | the safety limit stopped the attempt |
198	| `error` | the system stopped with an error |
199	| `no-enumeration` | the configuration has no mechanism for asking for more: the program printed what it computed for the stage and the stage ended (Python, ALGOL 60) |
200	
201	The execution state is classified **after** the call (section 5).
202	
203	### observe()
204	
205	Records the state the common observations need (`SPECIFICATION.md`,
206	"Observations common to every problem"), **verbatim**, as the system or
207	the program holds it at the end of the stage, including at the moment a
208	budget runs out: bindings held (`SPECIFICATION.md`, "reported": a binding
209	is reported if `observe()` can read it), residual relations, suspended
210	work, alternatives held. `observe.raw` is what was read, unedited;
211	`observe.bindings` splits it by unknown only where that can be done
212	mechanically. A residual counts as reported only if it is state that the
213	system or program holds and acts on later; printing the posed information
214	back is not observing it, and the harness never makes a residual up from
215	the posed information.
216	
217	### print()
218	
219	The system's own rendering of what it holds at the end of the stage (an
220	Absys assertion's printed derivations, a Prolog toplevel's bindings, the
221	program's printed values), recorded verbatim in `print`. The harness
222	never reformats it.
223	
224	### Observing must not consume the computation
225	
226	In a configuration where collecting answers or observing would end or
227	alter the computation that the next stage extends (exhausting a
228	backtracking search in a SWI-Prolog *session* engine, for instance),
229	`answers()` and `observe()` for stage k are taken on a **separate run of
230	stages 1 to k**, and the incremental computation is left as it was. The
231	record marks each such query `collected_on: "separate-run"`, and the
232	observation `taken_on: "separate-run"`, and keeps the separate run's
233	stdout, stderr and steps under `separate_run`. Its P11 effects go to the
234	observation log (section 6). In a reposed configuration every stage's run
235	is already separate, and nothing more is needed.
236	
237	## 5. Execution state
238	
239	Recorded per computation, per attempt, in the vocabulary of
240	`SPECIFICATION.md` ("Execution state"), **as far as the harness can tell
241	it mechanically**:
242	
243	| state | what the harness reads to say so |
244	|---|---|
245	| `budget` | its budget mechanism fired (Absys `--steps`, `call_with_inference_limit/3`, the `sys.monitoring` callback, `--max-steps`) |
246	| `timeout` | the safety limit stopped the attempt |
247	| `error` | the system stopped with an error; the error is copied verbatim to `error_verbatim` |
248	| `alternatives pending` | the system's own report that a request for more answers would resume it (a nondeterministic exit, open choicepoints, hibernating derivations), or, for Python and ALGOL 60, the program's named pending structure, read by `observe()` |
249	| `suspended` | the system's own report of held work that later information may resume (suspended equations, attributed variables with goals, a blocked engine, a program's named queue) |
250	| `finished` | the system stopped and reports none of the above |
251	
252	`alternatives pending` and `suspended` may both hold. `finished` excludes
253	the others; at most one of `budget`, `timeout` and `error` holds. Where
254	the harness cannot tell mechanically, it says so (`determined: false`),
255	lists what it could tell, and gives its basis. **The harness never
256	classifies the semantic axis, the representation, the simplification or
257	the effects class**: those are the classifiers' (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Roles"),
258	from the record.
259	
260	## 6. Commitments and the effects log (P11)
261	
262	**Commitments are preserved when a run is reposed.** At a commit stage
263	(`stages.json`, `commit: true`: P11c stage 3, P11d stage 2), the system
264	selects one of its current outcomes, v, and reports it through its
265	answers mechanism (`answers(1)`). The harness keeps that answer verbatim.
266	When a later stage is reposed, the commit stage is replayed **as the
267	information x = v**, with v passed to the program verbatim as first
268	selected, and recorded in `posed.replayed_commitments`. The harness never
269	asks the system to select again, and never parses or rewrites v beyond
270	taking the answer as the system gave it. Where the system did not select
271	(one that keeps every alternative live), nothing is replayed as a
272	commitment, and that is recorded; the classifiers judge it as P11 says.
273	In P11a and P11b, which have one stage, the outcome is committed when it
274	is reported (`committed_when_reported`).
275	
276	**The effects log.** The harness provides L and emit: one stub, with the
277	same behaviour and the same log format in every system (the binding of
278	emit into each language is the system harness's).
279	
280	- `emit(m)` appends one entry, m as the program passed it, rendered as
281	  the system renders m, to the log, and returns. It does nothing else: it
282	  does not fail, defer, buffer past the end of the stage, deduplicate, or
283	  read the log. Nothing the system does can remove an entry.
284	- The log is a file of JSON lines, one entry per line, with the fields of
285	  `effect_entry` in the schema: `seq` (position, from 1, never reused),
286	  `entry`, `run_id`, `stage`, `attempt`, `during_replay_of` (the earlier
287	  stage being replayed when emit was called, in a reposed run, else
288	  null), and `log`.
289	- **One classification log per configuration and instance**, at
290	  `results/<system>/<configuration>/P11/raw/<instance>.effects.jsonl`,
291	  **never reset**, across every behaviour run the harness makes, reposed
292	  runs and safety reruns included. The record copies the entries this run
293	  appended into each attempt's `effects`, and the whole log after the run
294	  into `effects.log_after_run`, with `entries_before_run`.
295	- **Separate observation runs** (section 4) and **every cost and storage
296	  run** write to `<instance>.effects-observation.jsonl` in the same
297	  folder, which is not judged (Q8).
298	- Entries emitted while replaying an earlier stage carry
299	  `during_replay_of`, so that entries duplicated only by reposing can be
300	  counted separately. The harness marks when an entry was made; whether it
301	  is a duplicate, and whether it was before, at or after commitment, is
302	  for the classifiers.
303	
304	## 7. Budget and safety limit
305	
306	| | P12, P13, P16 | every other problem |
307	|---|---|---|
308	| budget | 10⁸ steps per stage and computation | 10⁶ steps per stage and computation |
309	| safety limit | 600 s per stage, **fixed, no rerun** | 60 s per stage, then **one rerun at 600 s** |
310	| source | the problem file (`stages.json`, `limits`) | `PROTOCOL.md`, "Running" |
311	
312	- **Steps** are in the systems file's unit (Absys steps, SWI-Prolog
313	  inferences, Python bytecode instructions, ALGOL 60 interpreter ticks).
314	  The budget is a classification within a system, never compared across
315	  systems. Each spawned computation has its own budget; P16b stages 2
316	  and 3 have one for the whole.
317	- **A reposed run** has a budget of its **measured restart cost plus
318	  10⁶** (10⁸ where the problem says). The restart cost is always
319	  measured, in the system's step unit, never estimated or taken from
320	  another run (Q6):
321	  - **in-run** (the default): the harness reads the system's step count
322	    at the moment stage k is first posed in the reposed run, after the
323	    replay of stages 1 to k−1. That count is the restart cost, and the
324	    stage then has 10⁶ more steps: its budget is the restart cost plus
325	    10⁶. During the replay each replayed stage has the budget it had
326	    when first posed (10⁶ each);
327	  - **separate-run**, only where the system cannot read its count at that
328	    moment: the harness first runs stages 1 to k−1 alone, posed exactly
329	    as in the replay and with no `answers()` call, and measures its
330	    steps; that is the restart cost, and the reposed run's budget is it
331	    plus 10⁶.
332	
333	  It is recorded in `steps.restart_cost`, with `restart_cost_method`
334	  (`in-run` or `separate-run`) and `restart_cost_source`. The only
335	  exception is a configuration with no step count at all (ALGOL 60
336	  x1sim, Q12), whose records have `budget_enforced: false` and
337	  `restart_cost: null`.
338	- **After budget.** If stage k ends in *budget* and the configuration can
339	  keep its computation and continue it, stage k+1 is posed into that same
340	  computation, with a new budget (`continued_after_budget: true`). Only
341	  where it cannot are stages 1 to k+1 reposed (`reason: "after-budget"`),
342	  counted under restart cost. Whether a configuration can continue is the
343	  system harness's statement, in its README.
344	- **After error.** Stage k+1 is posed by reposing stages 1 to k+1
345	  (`reason: "after-error"`), counted under restart cost, in every
346	  configuration, incremental ones included.
347	- **After timeout.** As after error: the stopped computation cannot be
348	  continued, so stage k+1 is reposed (`reason: "after-timeout"`), Q7.
349	- **Safety limit.** It protects the harness; it is not a measurement.
350	  It covers one attempt of one stage: for an incremental stage, from
351	  posing stage k to the end of `print()`; for a reposed stage, the whole
352	  run of stages 1 to k. When it stops an attempt, the harness stops the
353	  system by the means its README gives (`safety_limit.how_stopped`),
354	  records the attempt with what it had collected, and, where the problem
355	  allows, **reruns the stage once** with the limit raised tenfold
356	  (attempt 2, `reason: "safety-rerun"`). An incremental configuration's
357	  rerun is reposed, since the stopped computation is gone. If the rerun
358	  also stops, *timeout* is final for that stage (`final-timeout`). Under
359	  a fixed limit (P12, P13, P16) the first stop is final
360	  (`fixed-limit-timeout`). **Both attempts are recorded.** Answers
361	  collected before a stop are kept and classified on the semantic axis;
362	  only the execution state is *timeout*.
363	- A run that hits the safety limit only because it is instrumented (cost
364	  or storage, where the behaviour run finished) is recorded as such; it
365	  is not evidence about the model (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Modes of running").
366	  The classifiers read that from the records of the two modes.
367	- **ALGOL 60 x1sim** has no step count, so no budget can be enforced;
368	  only the safety limit stops it, and its records say
369	  `budget_enforced: false` (Q12).
370	
371	## 8. Modes
372	
373	Each program is run in up to three modes, one run each. A run's record
374	says its mode, and each figure is taken from the mode that gives it:
375	
376	| mode | instrumentation | gives |
377	|---|---|---|
378	| **behaviour** | none beyond the harness (its budget counter included) | answers, observe(), print(), the execution state, the effects log. **The semantic result and the execution state are taken from this run** |
379	| **cost** | step counting only | steps per stage (incremental and restated), restart cost, answer latency (steps to the first answer, between answers, to the end), problem operations, repeated work where the systems file names a source, candidates examined (P12) |
380	| **storage** | the systems file's storage measurement | store vector (boundary and peak), retained alternatives (at answers, at boundaries, at budget, peak), suspended state (at boundaries and peak), P13's maximum resident set size where the systems file takes it from a separate run |
381	
382	- **A sampled measurement is never taken from the run that gives the step
383	  count or the classification.** A sampled maximum (`peak.kind =
384	  "sampled"`) may appear only in a storage record; `validate.py` rejects
385	  one in a behaviour or cost record. Exact peaks may appear in any mode
386	  whose instrumentation gives them.
387	- A field a mode does not measure is `null`, or `{}` for the store
388	  vector. Figures that a mode records incidentally (the budget counter's
389	  steps in a behaviour run) are kept, but the figure of record is the one
390	  from the mode in this table.
391	- Where two modes can be compared, their answers must agree; a
392	  disagreement is reported as a fault of the instrumentation, by the
393	  classifiers, from the records.
394	- The systems file says which modes a configuration has (x1sim:
395	  behaviour only). P13's process CPU time and maximum resident set size
396	  are recorded where the systems file says, for growth only.
397	
398	## 9. The raw record
399	
400	One JSON file per run, valid against [`record.schema.json`](record.schema.json),
401	the same for every system. Every string the system produced is kept
402	**verbatim** (JSON-escaped, never trimmed, reflowed or decoded beyond the
403	system's own output encoding; bytes that are not UTF-8 are written as
404	`�` and noted in `harness_faults`). A value the harness could not
405	read is `null`, never estimated.
406	
407	### Run metadata (`run`)
408

450	### Rules a record must keep (checked by `validate.py`)
451	
452	Beyond the schema:
453	
454	1. The instance exists in `stages.json`, with the same problem,
455	   sub-problem and parameters, and the problem's limits; a complete run
456	   has every stage, numbered 1 … K.
457	2. Each stage's queries are those of `stages.json`, on the computations it
458	   names, with its caps; spawned computations are those it spawns, in the
459	   instance's `spawn_order` (or the P16b fallback).
460	3. No query has more answers than its cap; `ended_by: "cap"` has exactly
461	   cap answers; `ended_by` budget, timeout or error appears in the
462	   computation's state.
463	4. Stage 1 is `fresh`. A reposed stage replays exactly 1 … k−1. An
464	   incremental stage replays nothing, and is not used in a reposing
465	   configuration except to continue after budget. After an error the next
466	   stage is reposed. A `continued_after_budget` stage follows a *budget*.
467	5. A reposed stage has a measured restart cost, with its method, and
468	   its budget is that plus the problem's budget; any other stage's is the
469	   problem's budget. Only a computation with `budget_enforced: false`
470	   may have no restart cost.
471	6. A second attempt exists only after the safety limit stopped the first,
472	   under the problem's rerun limit; none under a fixed limit. A *timeout*
473	   state and a safety-limit stop go together.
474	7. `finished` stands alone; at most one of budget, timeout, error;
475	   *error* has its text; *budget* matches `budget_exhausted`.
476	8. No sampled maximum outside a storage record.
477	9. A separate run, where one is used, replays 1 … k.
478	10. P11 records have `effects`; others do not. The entries of the
479	    attempts are exactly the classification log's entries after
480	    `entries_before_run`; cost and storage runs write only to the
481	    observation log; replayed commitments are for earlier commit stages.
482	
483	```
484	python3 harnesses/validate.py results/<system>/<configuration>/<problem>/raw/*.json
485	python3 harnesses/validate.py --check-stages            # checks stages.json itself
486	python3 harnesses/validate.py --stages harnesses/examples/stages-made-up.json harnesses/examples/made-up-*.json
487	```
488	
489	The last line runs on the made-up examples: three valid records (an
490	incremental run with a safety-limit rerun; a reposing run with a commit
491	and the effects log; two spawned computations in a storage run with a
492	separate observation run) and one deliberately invalid record, which it
493	rejects with six errors.

508	## 11. What a program must provide
509	
510	A program author cannot run anything before the program is fixed (only
511	the system harness's `check`, which executes nothing). So each system
512	harness's README says exactly, per configuration, how a program meets
513	these requirements; the common part is:
514	
515	1. **Stages as units the harness can pose.** The program handles stage k
516	   when, and only when, the harness poses it, in the way the
517	   configuration receives stages (incremental, or by replaying 1 … k).
518	   Code for stage k does not depend on any later stage.
519	2. **Replay.** In a reposed run the program carries out every stage
520	   1 … k in order, replacements and withdrawals included, and accepts a
521	   replayed commit stage as the information x = v, with v as the harness
522	   passes it (the verbatim answer of the commit stage).
523	3. **Instance parameters.** The program takes n, an arrival order, a
524	   spawn order or the answer mode from the harness, as `stages.json`
525	   names them, and holds everything else.
526	4. **Answers through the standard mechanism.** Answers reach the harness
527	   only through the configuration's standard mechanism for answers, in
528	   the form the system harness's README fixes (for Python and ALGOL 60,
529	   printed lines with the delimiters it defines).
530	5. **State for observe().** Whatever the system does not expose by
531	   itself (a Python program's named pending structure, its counters of
532	   problem operations), the program exposes in the form the system
533	   harness reads. Counters that only count are H (`METRICS.md`).
534	6. **Constants for the verifier** (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Writing a program",
535	   rule 6). Every constant of every stage is in **one** place the
536	   verifier can replace without touching anything else, and the program
537	   stays correct for other constants. Which place is fixed per system by
538	   its harness README, not here, with this default:
539	
540	   | system | where the constants are |
541	   |---|---|
542	   | ALGOL 60 | **input**: read with the input procedures as integers in the problem's encoding (`systems/algol-60/README.md`, "Values"), from a constants file the harness passes; recorded as `constants.how = "input"` with its SHA-256 |
543	   | Absys, SWI-Prolog, Python | **one marked constants block** in the program, between a line containing `CONSTANTS BEGIN` and a line containing `CONSTANTS END`, each inside a comment of the language, holding nothing but the constants, or **input**, as the system harness decides and documents; recorded as `block` or `input` |
544	
545	   A sub-problem with no constants (P04d, P04f, P08b; `variants/README.md`)
546	   records `none`. Sizes n and arrival orders are not constants (they are
547	   not varied) and come from the harness (point 3).
548	7. **Provenance** (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Writing a program", rules 1, 2, 8): its
549	   author, whether the author had seen a precursor, and the source of each
550	   idiom, in a comment the system harness README places.
551	
552	**H tokens** (`METRICS.md`, class H) are the per-system harness's own
553	calls as they appear in a program: the calls that pose stages, request
554	answers and print, the emit stub's binding, and output adapters (rule
555	13). Each system harness's README lists them, construct by construct,
556	before any program is written. Code a program adds beyond them is
557	classed by the rules of `METRICS.md`, not as H.

48	## 2. The program contract
49	
50	An author who cannot run the program before its results are taken writes it
51	to this section, and may use only `check` (section 6) before it is fixed.
52	
53	### 2.1 File layout
54	
55	- **One file**, the whole program: one ALGOL 60 program (a block or compound
56	  statement). Any extension; the harness copies it as `prog.a60` for x1sim.
57	- **Constants** (common contract, section 11.6): every constant of every stage
58	  is in **one input file**, beside the program, with the same name and the
59	  extension `.constants` (`P07c.alg` → `P07c.constants`). The verifier
60	  substitutes a hidden variant by passing another file in the environment
61	  variable `ALGOL60_CONSTANTS` (and its id in `ALGOL60_VARIANT`); the program
62	  is not touched. **Every line of the file is tagged with the stage that
63	  first uses it**: `k: v1 v2 …`, where k is a stage of the instance (1..K)
64	  and the values are integers in the problem's encoding
65	  (`systems/algol-60/README.md`, Values), separated by spaces, in a layout the
66	  program states in a comment. A stage may have several lines, or none;
67	  blank lines are ignored; any other line is refused (exit 2). The harness
68	  sends stage k's lines **only with the message that poses or replays stage
69	  k** (2.2): no stage's constants are on the program's input before that
70	  stage is posed (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Writing a program", rule 5, no
71	  anticipation). A constant a later stage uses again is kept by the program
72	  from the stage that first gave it. The program must stay correct for other
73	  constants: give lengths in the file, never in the program. A sub-problem with no constants has no file (`constants.how =
74	  "none"`). The program holds nothing else of the stages.
75	- **Representation**:
76	  - *report*: as `algol60` reads it: reserved words in lower case
77	    (`begin`, `if`), or quote-stropped, or underlined; strings `"..."` (with
78	    `\n`) or `` `...' ``. The procedures `ininteger`, `outinteger`,
79	    `outstring` are IFIP's, and are external mechanisms in report
80	    (systems file, Configurations).
81	  - *x1sim*: as the X1 compiler reads it: **underlined reserved words**
82	    (each letter followed by U+0332, `b̲e̲g̲i̲n̲`), strings only `` `...' ``,
83	    the operators as symbols (`¬ ∧ ∨ ⊃ ≡ ≠ ≤ ≥ × ÷`; underlined `not` or `and`
84	    are refused), and the X1 system's procedures `read`, `print`,
85	    `PRINTTEXT`, `NLCR`, `SPACE`, `TAB` (no `ininteger` or `outstring`).
86	    Characters in strings: letters, digits, space and `[ ] / = : , . ( ) + -`
87	    (the X1 code has no `#`, `@`, `<` inside text is risky). The X1 system
88	    breaks a line at 144 positions: print `NLCR` between answers so that
89	    no tag is split.
90	  - *x1*: `algol60 --x1` reads both forms and has both sets of procedures.
91	    A program in the x1sim form runs unchanged in x1 (the qualification does
92	    this); a program in the report form runs in x1 too.
93	- **Declarations, in comments** (comments are not tokens). An ALGOL 60
94	  comment ends at the first `;`, so none of these may contain `;`:
95	
96	      comment HARNESS POSING incremental;          (or: reposed — exactly one, required)
97	      comment PROVENANCE author: ...;
98	      comment PROVENANCE precursor seen: yes|no;
99	      comment PROVENANCE idioms: <each idiom and its source>;
100	      comment CONSTANTS <the layout of the constants file>;
101	
102	  `run` and `check` read the posing declaration from the program's bytes,
103	  and refuse a program without exactly one (exit 2).
104	
105	### 2.2 How the program learns which stage to handle: its input
106	
107	The harness writes everything on the program's **standard input**, as lines
108	of integers, read with the configuration's input procedure
109	(`ininteger(0, v)` in report and x1; `v := read` in x1 and x1sim):
110	
111	1. **The instance line**, first: `n a m c1 … cm`
112	   - `n` the instance's size (`stages.json` parameter `n`), else 0;
113	   - `a` its answer cap where the instance gives one (P12: 20 for `all`,
114	     1 for `any-one`), else 0;
115	   - `m` the number of codes that follow, and `c1 … cm` the instance's
116	     `order` or `spawn_order`, each as its code (table below), else `m = 0`.
117	2. **Messages**, one per line, each **followed by the constants lines of
118	   the stage it poses or replays** (the lines of the file tagged `k:`, in
119	   file order, with the tag removed and the values verbatim; nothing if the
120	   stage has none). The program reads exactly that stage's constants after
121	   reading the message's words:
122	
123	   | message | meaning |
124	   |---|---|
125	   | `1 k` | **pose stage k**: stage k's information arrives (in an incremental program, into the computation that holds stages 1..k−1; in a reposed run, the stage posed after the replay) |
126	   | `2 j` | **replay stage j** (reposed run only): carry out stage j again, as when it was posed, replacements and withdrawals included |
127	   | `3 j` then a line `v` | **replay commit stage j as the information x = v** (P11, reposed run): `v` is the commit stage's first answer, verbatim as it was printed (the text between `[answer]` and `[/answer]`), then stage j's constants lines. Print P11 answers so that they can be read back (as integers) |
128	   | `4 k c` | **spawn computation c of stage k** (P09a, P09b): start computation c and run it to its end; stage k's constants follow each spawn message |
129	
130	   The program answers **every message with exactly one `[end]`** (2.3),
131	   printed when it has finished with that message, and then reads its next
132	   message. It never reads input beyond the message it is handling: in an
133	   incremental run the next message is written only after `[end]`, so a read
134	   beyond it waits forever (and the stage ends at the safety limit). After the
135	   last stage the harness closes the input; the program's next read then
136	   fails with the interpreter's "the input is exhausted" (x1sim: "No input"),
137	   which ends the process. That is expected, not an error of the stage.
138	
139	   No message says how many stages follow (no anticipation).
140	
141	**Incremental program** (`HARNESS POSING incremental`; the systems file's
142	"read each stage with ininteger or insymbol as it arrives, which counts as
143	the same computation"): a loop that reads a message, handles it, prints the
144	stage's answers and observe block, prints `[end]`, and reads the next. It
145	must also accept `2 j` and `3 j` (handled as `1 j`, and as x = v): the
146	harness reposes an incremental program after a budget, error or safety stop.
147	Stage 1 arrives as `1 1`.
148	
149	**Reposed program** (`HARNESS POSING reposed`; "otherwise each stage is
150	posed by rerunning with stages 1 to k"): for stage k the harness starts the
151	program afresh and writes, at once, `2 1` … `2 k−1` (with `3 j` + `v` for a
152	commit stage) and then `1 k`. The program reads messages until it reads a
153	`1`, printing `[end]` after each replayed one, then computes stage k, prints
154	its answers and observe block and a final `[end]`, and may end.
155	
156	Codes of `order`, `spawn_order` and computations (by first appearance in
157	`stages.json`; structure, not constants):
158	
159	| instance or stage | what | codes |
160	|---|---|---|
161	| P02b | `order` | R1 = 1, R2 = 2, R3 = 3 |
162	| P07a | `order` | 1 = 1, 2 = 2, 3 = 3 |
163	| P09a, P09b | `spawn_order` | A = 1, B = 2 |
164	| P09a, P09b stage 1 | computation `c` of `4 1 c` | A = 1, B = 2 |
165	| P16a | `order` | ascending = 1, descending = 2, interleaved = 3 |
166	| P16b, P16c, P16d, P16d2 | `order` | ascending = 1 |
167	| P16b stage 1 | computations C1–C4 | **not spawned**: posed as `1 1` to `main` (`spawn_fallback`, QUESTIONS.md A3) |
168	
169	So `P12c.n16.any` gives the line `16 1 0`, `P09a.BA` gives `0 0 2 2 1`
170	followed by `4 1 2` and later `4 1 1`, and `P16a.n100.descending` gives
171	`100 0 1 2`.
172	
173	### 2.3 How the program reports: tags in its output
174	
175	Answers reach the harness through the system's standard mechanism, the values
176	the program prints (systems file; `PROTOCOL.md`). The program prints them,
177	with `outstring`/`outinteger` (report) or `PRINTTEXT`/`print` (x1sim), between
178	these tags. The harness keeps the text between tags **verbatim** (the
179	padding of `outinteger` and of the X1 `print` included):
180	
181	| tag | meaning |
182	|---|---|
183	| `[answer]TEXT[/answer]` | one answer to the query of the computation now running. In order; the first `cap` are collected (`stages.json` gives the cap of each query), any more stay in `stdout` and `print` |
184	| `[observe]TEXT[/observe]` | the state for `observe()` at the end of the stage (2.4). Print it once, after the answers |
185	| `[emit]TEXT[/emit]` | the effect stub `emit(TEXT)` (P11, 2.5) |
186	| `[end]` | the program has finished with the current message. Print a newline *before* it, nothing after it before the next read |
187	
188	The text of a tag must not contain the tags themselves.
189	
190	### 2.4 observe() and the execution state
191	
192	ALGOL 60 has no unknowns, alternatives or suspension of its own, so
193	`observe()` reads what the program prints in its observe block, and the
194	execution state is read from it. Inside `[observe]…[/observe]`, any text
195	(the held relations, a residual, the program's named structures) is kept
196	verbatim in `observe.raw`; these tags are also read mechanically:
197	
198	| inside observe | recorded as |
199	|---|---|
200	| `[bind NAME]VALUE[/bind]` | `observe.bindings[NAME] = VALUE` |
201	| `[alternatives NAME COUNT]` | `alternatives.by_type[NAME]`; `at_boundary` is their sum; a sum above 0 is the state **alternatives pending** |
202	| `[held-as all-live]` (`backtracking`, `mixed`) | `alternatives.held_as` (else `unknown` if alternatives are reported, `none` if not) |
203	| `[problem-alternatives NAME COUNT]` | `alternatives.problem_defined[NAME]` (METRICS.md: P05's values of x, P12's partial sequences, P15a's interleavings) |
204	| `[suspended NAME COUNT]` | `suspended.items[NAME]`; `at_boundary` their sum; a sum above 0 is the state **suspended** |
205	| `[operations NAME COUNT]` | `problem_operations[NAME]`: applications of each case of each relation (`conc/1`), counted by the program **since the computation started** |
206	| `[candidates COUNT]` | `candidates_examined` (P12) |
207	
208	COUNT is an integer, printed with `outinteger` or `print` (a leading `+` and
209	spaces are accepted). A stage that ends with `[end]` (or with the program's
210	normal end) and reports neither alternatives nor suspended work is
211	**finished**. **budget**: the interpreter reported `stopped after N steps`.
212	**error**: the process ended otherwise before `[end]`; `error_verbatim` is
213	the interpreter's message (its last line of standard error; for x1sim all of
214	standard error). **timeout**: the safety limit. When a stage ends by budget,
215	error or timeout, the program cannot print an observe block at that moment;
216	whatever it printed in the stage before the stop is what is recorded.
217	
218	`print()` is the stage's output, verbatim, from its message to its `[end]`.
219	
220	### 2.5 emit and commitments (P11)
221	
222	`emit(m)` is bound as printing `[emit]m[/emit]`. The harness appends `m`,
223	verbatim, to the effects log when it reads it, with the run, stage, attempt
224	and (in a reposed run) the stage being replayed (`during_replay_of`). The
225	log is `OUTDIR/<instance>.effects.jsonl` in behaviour mode, and
226	`OUTDIR/<instance>.effects-observation.jsonl` in cost and storage mode; it
227	is never reset. The interpreter holds its output until it next reads input
228	(or ends), so an emit is logged by the end of its stage at the latest.
229	
230	At a commit stage the program selects one outcome and prints it as the
231	stage's answer. That answer, verbatim, is v: a later reposed run sends
232	`3 j` and then v on its own line, and the program takes it as x = v without
233	selecting again.
234	
235	### 2.6 spawn (P09a, P09b)
236	
237	ALGOL 60 has no separate computations. A spawned computation is a part of
238	the one program (a procedure, typically), started by the message `4 k c`.
239	It runs to its end, budget or error, and prints `[end]`; then the harness
240	spawns the next, in the instance's `spawn_order` (`side_by_side: false`).
241	They share the program's variables. Each has its own budget (report, x1). If
242	one ends the process (budget, error, timeout), the ones after it in the stage
243	are recorded as not started (QUESTIONS.md A3).
244	
245	### 2.7 H tokens
246	
247	These constructs are **H** (`METRICS.md`, class H, rule 13), every token of
248	each:
249	
250	1. each statement that reads a harness word: the instance line
251	   (`ininteger(0, n)`, `n := read`, the loop that reads the codes), a message
252	   word (code, stage number, computation code), and the statement that reads
253	   the replayed value v (turning v into the information x = v is classed by
254	   METRICS.md, not H);
255	2. the message loop: its `for … while …` header (or label and `go to`), and
256	   the tests and connectives that select by the message code, by k (which
257	   stage's code to run) and by c (which computation): the dispatch, not the
258	   stage code it selects;
259	3. every output statement whose only effect is to print a tag or the text
260	   inside a tag (`[answer]`, `[observe]` and its inner tags, `[emit]`,
261	   `[end]`, and the `NLCR` that separate them), and procedures whose only
262	   effect is to print answers or state the program already holds (output
263	   adapters);
264	4. counters that only count (problem operations, candidates): their
265	   declarations and increments;
266	5. declarations of variables that hold only harness words (the message code,
267	   the stage number k, the computation code c, a loop variable of the message
268	   loop).
269	
270	Not H: the variables holding instance parameters as the program uses them
271	(n, an order, the cap), reading the constants (that is the stage
272	information, P), holding information between stages, and any pending or
273	suspension structure (R or S by METRICS.md rule 19).
274	
275	### 2.8 A complete minimal example
276	
277	Made-up problem **X01** (not one of P01–P16): one unknown integer x; stage 1
278	gives x ≥ c1, stage 2 gives x ≤ c2, stage 3 gives x ≠ c3; the query is every
279	x. Program `qualification/programs/x01-incremental.alg`, configuration
280	report:
281	
282	```
283	begin
284	  comment HARNESS POSING incremental;
285	  comment PROVENANCE author: harness-algol-60 (the harness README's example, for the made-up problem X01, not a result);
286	  comment PROVENANCE precursor seen: no;
287	  comment PROVENANCE idioms: the Revised Report (1962), and the input and output procedures of the interpreter (IFIP 1964, Modified Report 1976);
288	  comment X01 (made up). One unknown integer x. Stage 1: x >= c1. Stage 2: x <= c2. Stage 3: x differs from c3. Query: every x. Constants file: a line 1: c1, a line 2: c2, a line 3: c3, each read when its stage is posed;
289	  integer n, cap, m, i, code, k, c1, c2, c3, lo, hi, ex, x, tested, held;
290	  Boolean haslo, hashi, hasex;
291	
292	  comment harness words: the instance parameters;
293	  ininteger(0, n); ininteger(0, cap); ininteger(0, m);
294	  for i := 1 step 1 until m do ininteger(0, code);
295	  haslo := hashi := hasex := false; tested := 0;
296	
297	  for i := 1 while true do
298	  begin
299	    comment harness words: one message, the stage to pose, and then that stage's constants;
300	    ininteger(0, code); ininteger(0, k);
301	    if k = 1 then begin ininteger(0, c1); lo := c1; haslo := true end
302	    else if k = 2 then begin ininteger(0, c2); hi := c2; hashi := true end
303	    else if k = 3 then begin ininteger(0, c3); ex := c3; hasex := true end;
304	
305	    comment the query: every x, when the relations bound it on both sides;
306	    if haslo and hashi then
307	      for x := lo step 1 until hi do
308	      begin
309	        tested := tested + 1;
310	        if not (hasex and x = ex) then
311	        begin outstring(1, "[answer]x = "); outinteger(1, x); outstring(1, "[/answer]\n") end
312	      end;
313	
314	    comment observe: the relations held, and how many wait for more information;
315	    held := (if haslo then 1 else 0) + (if hashi then 1 else 0) + (if hasex then 1 else 0);
316	    outstring(1, "[observe]");
317	    if haslo then begin outstring(1, "x >= "); outinteger(1, lo) end;
318	    if hashi then begin outstring(1, "x <= "); outinteger(1, hi) end;
319	    if hasex then begin outstring(1, "x <> "); outinteger(1, ex) end;
320	    if not (haslo and hashi) then
321	    begin outstring(1, "[suspended held-relations "); outinteger(1, held); outstring(1, "]") end;
322	    outstring(1, "[operations x-tested "); outinteger(1, tested); outstring(1, "]");
323	    outstring(1, "[/observe]\n[end]")
324	  end
325	end
326	```
327	
328	Its constants file `x01-incremental.constants` is
329	
330	    1: 3
331	    2: 9
332	    3: 5
333	
334	The harness writes `0 0 0` and `1 1` with `3`; after the first `[end]`,
335	`1 2` with `9`; after the second, `1 3` with `5`; then it closes the input. It records: stage 1, no
336	answers, state suspended (`held-relations 1`); stage 2, the seven answers
337	`x = 3 ` … `x = 9 `, finished; stage 3, six answers. H here: the reads of
338	`n, cap, m`, the code loop, the message reads, the `for i := 1 while true`
339	header, the `if k = …` tests and connectives, every `outstring`/`outinteger`
340	of a tag, the counter `tested` and its statement, and the declarations of
341	`code, k, i, tested, held`; the rest (the reads of `c1`, `c2`, `c3`
342	included: they are the stage information) is classed by METRICS.md. The same
343	problem, posed by rerunning, is `x01-reposed.alg`; in the X1 form, for x1 and
344	x1sim, `x01-x1.a60` and `x01-x1-reposed.a60`.
345	
346	---
347	
348	## 3. How the harness drives the system
349	
350	### 3.1 report and x1: a process per stage, re-created
351	
352	`--max-steps` is fixed when the interpreter starts and counts from the start
353	of the process, and the interpreter reports its count only when the limit
354	stops it. So, to give every stage and every spawned computation its own
355	budget of exactly 10⁶ steps (10⁸ for P12, P13, P16), the harness runs each
356	in its own process: for stage k of an incremental program it starts the
357	interpreter with `--max-steps R(k−1) + budget`, writes the instance line and
358	constants and `1 1`, waits for `[end]`, writes `1 2`, … and finally `1 k`.
359	The program receives every stage as it first arrived, one after another,
360	into one computation; the earlier stages are re-created, not replayed, and
361	the record says `posed.how = "incremental"` with nothing replayed (QUESTIONS.md
362	A2). **Every such attempt is marked**: its `notes` begin with a line
363	
364	    recreated_for_budget: true; computation: main; prefix_messages: 2; prefix_stages: [1, 2]; prefix_steps: 103; prefix_commit_stages_carried_out_again: []
365	
366	(the schema has no field for it, so it is a note in this fixed form).
367	`prefix_steps` is R(k−1), the steps of the re-created prefix: they are **not
368	charged to the stage** (`steps.stage` and the budget count from the end of
369	the prefix; `restart_cost` is null; `steps.restated` includes them, as
370	"from nothing"). A commit stage in the re-created prefix is carried out
371	again by the program, deterministically, and listed in
372	`prefix_commit_stages_carried_out_again`; its output (v included) is checked
373	byte-identical to the first time. This relies on the interpreter being deterministic (it has no clock and
374	no random numbers): the earlier stages' output in the new process must be
375	byte-identical to what was recorded for them, or the run has a harness fault.
376	Their output is not repeated in the attempt's `stdout`, and their emits are
377	not logged again.
378	
379	**Steps** are read only through `--max-steps`, by bisection: R(k), the steps
380	until the program asks for input after stage k (or ends), is the least limit
381	at which a run of stages 1..k, its input closed after stage k's `[end]`, is
382	not stopped with `stopped after N steps`. Each probe is a run of the program
383	(their number is in the record's notes). The stage's incremental cost is
384	R(k) − R(k−1), its restated cost R(k).
385	
386	**A reposed stage** (a reposed program; or an incremental one after budget,
387	error or timeout, and every safety rerun after stage 1): one new process,
388	all messages written at once. Its restart cost is measured as a separate run
389	(`restart_cost_method: "separate-run"`): the least limit at which stages
390	1..k−1 alone (their messages, then the input closed) are not stopped. The
391	budget is that plus 10⁶ (10⁸). The replay as a whole has at most the sum of
392	its stages' budgets (QUESTIONS.md A6).
393	
394	### 3.2 x1sim: one live process
395	
396	No step count, no limit. An incremental program runs in **one x1sim
397	process** for the whole run: the harness writes each message after the
398	previous `[end]`, and the computation is genuinely the same. A reposed stage
399	starts a new process with all its messages. x1sim writes its object file
400	beside the program, so it runs in a fresh temporary directory with a copy
401	`prog.a60`, `HOME` set there and `X1ALGOL_LIB` unset, so the library is
402	`/usr/local/lib/x1algol.lib`.
403	
404	### 3.3 Safety limit
405	
406	60 s per attempt (600 s for P12, P13, P16), as `stages.json` gives. For an
407	incremental attempt it runs from writing the stage's message to its `[end]`
408	(the re-created earlier stages are not inside it: they are guarded at 900 s
409	as a harness fault); for a reposed attempt it covers the whole run (Q13).
410	The harness stops the system with **SIGKILL to its process group**
411	(`how_stopped`), keeps what had been printed, and reruns once at the raised
412	limit (reposed; for stage 1, fresh) where the problem allows, else the stop
413	is final (`fixed-limit-timeout`). The interpreter flushes its output at every
414	read of input, at an error and at the step limit, but not when killed:
415	output printed but not yet flushed when the safety limit kills it is lost.
416	
417	### 3.4 Modes
418	
419	| mode | report, x1 | x1sim |
420	|---|---|---|
421	| behaviour | `algol60` with the budget's `--max-steps`; steps are measured only where a later budget needs them | `x1sim`, no budget |
422	| cost | as behaviour, plus R(k) at every stage, `steps_at` for each collected answer (the least limit at which the answer's `[/answer]` is in the output), `to_first_answer`, `between_answers`, `to_end`; repeated work from one extra run of `algol60-measure --measure` per computation | refused |
423	| storage | `algol60-measure --measure` for the attempt (its steps, under `--max-steps`, are the baseline's: systems file) | refused |
424	
425	**Store** (storage mode): `--measure` reports at the end of the process,
426	after the interpreter has unwound. The totals (`frames_made`, `calls`,
427	`name_uses`, `name_evaluations`, `name_first_evaluations`,
428	`name_repeat_evaluations`) are read as the stage boundary's, since the
429	process ends there; the live quantities (`frames`, `slots`, `arrays`,
430	`array_elements`, `names`, `call_depth`) have `boundary: null`, and their
431	peak over the process (stages 1..k) is recorded as the stage's (`exact`)
432	only where it exceeds the peak at the end of stage k−1, else `null`; a
433	reposed stage's peak is its run's. **Repeated work** is
434	`name_repeat_evaluations` (with first and all evaluations) between the
435	boundaries, or over the whole reposed run. **P13**: `cpu_time_s` and
436	`max_rss_kb` are the attempt process's, from `wait4`, in behaviour and cost
437	mode (not storage, which is instrumented).
438	
439	### 3.5 Confounds
440	
441	Everything the harness does beyond passing stages in, collecting answers and
442	reading state (copied into every record's `run.confounds`):
443	
444	1. the re-creation of the computation in report and x1 (3.1): an attempt
445	   in a fresh process, re-created for its budget, recorded as incremental
446	   and marked `recreated_for_budget: true` with its `prefix_steps`, which
447	   are not charged to the stage; its determinism check; a commit stage in
448	   the re-created prefix is carried out again by the program,
449	   deterministically, its output (v included) checked identical, and listed
450	   in the mark;
451	2. the bisection probes, extra runs of the program, for every step count;
452	3. closing the input after the stage under test, which ends the process with
453	   the interpreter's "input is exhausted" error after `[end]`;
454	4. the safety limit of an incremental attempt excludes the re-created stages;
455	5. output still in the interpreter's buffer at a safety-limit kill is lost;
456	6. store and repeated work read from the end-of-process report of the
457	   measurement build, with the peak attribution of 3.4;
458	7. the instance line and messages written on standard input, each message
459	   followed by its stage's constants lines with their `k:` tag removed;
460	8. answers, observe state, emits and stage ends read from printed tags by
461	   pattern matching; answers beyond the cap left uncollected;
462	9. spawned computations are parts of one program, run one after another;
463	10. x1sim: run in a temporary directory on a copy of the program, and no
464	    budget.
465	
466	---
467	
468	## 4. Records
469	
470	`run` writes `OUTDIR/<instance>.<mode>.<UTC>.json`, then validates it with
471	`harnesses/validate.py`; an invalid record is kept as `….INVALID.json` and
472	`run` exits 3. Exit 0 whatever the outcome of the stages; 2 for a usage error
473	(unknown configuration, instance or mode, a mode x1sim does not have, no
474	posing declaration), with no record. `PROGRAM` and `OUTDIR` are relative to
475	the repository root. `system_build.commit` is read from `/opt/src/COMMITS`;
476	the image digest from `HARNESS_IMAGE` if the launcher passes it, else null.
477	`HARNESS_PURPOSE` sets `run.purpose` (`primary` by default); `HARNESS_STAGES`
478	another stages file (only the qualification uses it).
479	
480	---
481	
482	## 5. check
483	
484	`harnesses/algol-60/check CONFIGURATION PROGRAM`:
485	
486	| configuration | what it runs |
487	|---|---|
488	| report | `algol60 --check PROGRAM`: parses and compiles, reports errors and warnings, runs nothing |
489	| x1 | `algol60 --x1 --check PROGRAM`, the same in the X1 dialect |
490	| x1sim | `x1algc prog.a60 /usr/local/lib/x1algol.lib` on a copy, in a temporary directory: the X1 compiler alone; the object code is discarded and the simulator is never started. On failure the compiler's report (which it writes on standard output) is printed |
491	
492	It also reports whether the posing declaration is present and whether a
493	constants file is beside the program. Messages are printed verbatim; exit 0
494	if none is an error, 1 otherwise. It poses no stage and prints nothing the
495	program would compute. The X1 compiler finds fewer errors than `algol60
496	--check` (it accepted `k := 1 +;`, which then stopped at run time); an x1sim
497	author may also check the program in x1. The qualification (E1–E2) shows a
498	program whose only effect is to print a marker leaves no marker and no file
499	when checked, in all three configurations.
500	
501	---
502	
503	## 6. Qualification
504	
505	`qualification/qualify.py`, run in the image from the repository root,
506	reruns all of it on made-up programs and problems (X01–X09,
507	`qualification/stages-made-up.json`) and writes its records to
508	`qualification/records/<UTC>/`. Its output is `qualification/output.txt`.
509	It shows: (A) the system run directly and the harness agree on each stage's
510	output and answers, the harness's step counts agree with `--max-steps`
511	itself (R passes, R−1 stops), the systems file's step examples (3, 3, 5, 1)
512	are reproduced as stage-step differences, and the storage figures equal
513	`--measure` run directly; (B) incremental and reposed programs give the same
514	answers in all three configurations, a commitment is replayed verbatim, the
515	modes agree, spawn follows the instance's order; (C) budget, error, safety
516	rerun, final and fixed-limit timeouts and usage errors; (D) every record
517	passes `validate.py`; (E) `check` executes nothing; (F) from a trace of
518	every write the harness made to the system's input (`HARNESS_INPUT_TRACE`,
519	qualification only), no stage's constants were on the input before its
520	message, in every process (attempts and probes), and every re-created stage
521	is marked with its `prefix_steps`.
522

# S mechanisms of the ALGOL 60 configurations

*Phase 4, before any program is run (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Recording a result":
every configuration's S mechanisms are listed, with their size). Class S is
code that implements a mechanism the configuration lacks (`METRICS.md`,
class S, rules 12 and 19).*

The systems file (`systems/algol-60/README.md`) admits supporting code for
every ALGOL 60 configuration: "ALGOL 60 has no unknowns, no relations and no
alternatives of its own … Some problems may be *not expressible* without
supporting code. That is a result." It names no supporting code that the
configurations provide, and none has been written for this study.

| configuration | S mechanisms provided | size |
|---|---|---|
| **report** | none | 0 tokens |
| **x1** | none | 0 tokens |
| **x1sim** | none | 0 tokens |

So every configuration of ALGOL 60 is, for this study, its **core** only
(the Revised Report, with the input and output procedures listed as external
mechanisms in report, and the X1 system's own procedures in x1 and x1sim). A
program that needs a mechanism ALGOL 60 lacks (a constraint store or
propagator general over relations, a unifier, a scheduler, a search) and
writes it is, by `METRICS.md` rule 19, in an *extended* configuration named
by that mechanism; since no such mechanism is listed here, such a program is
reported as a named variant, and the problem is *not expressible* in the
configuration as listed.

What is **not** S, so that it is not mistaken for it:

- the harness's own constructs in a program (reading the instance line and
  messages, the message dispatch, the printed tags, `emit`'s binding, output
  adapters, counters): these are **H**, listed in `README.md`, section 2.7;
- the input and output procedures (`ininteger`, `outinteger`, `outstring`;
  `read`, `print`, `PRINTTEXT`, `NLCR`): external mechanisms of the
  configuration (report), or the X1 system's own (x1, x1sim), counted as
  their call tokens;
- code written for one problem's own relations that holds them until their
  values arrive: **R**, in the core configuration (`METRICS.md` rule 19).

The harness itself (`run`) supplies no mechanism to any program: it passes
stages in and reads what the program prints (`README.md`, section 3.5).

1	# Questions for the ALGOL 60 harness, and the readings implemented
2	
3	*Harness author, ALGOL 60, wave 1, against `spec-1.0`. No frozen file and no
4	file outside `harnesses/algol-60/` was changed. Each entry says what could not
5	be implemented as written for ALGOL 60, or was open, and the reading this
6	harness implements. The common part's readings (`harnesses/QUESTIONS.md`,
7	Q1–Q19) are implemented as written, except where an entry here says so.*
8	
9	## A1. The systems file's probes are not files
10	
11	The brief asks to qualify on "the systems file's probes", and
12	`systems/algol-60/` holds only `README.md`. Its Units section gives four step
13	examples ("`i := 1; i := 2` in a block is 3 steps", a procedure statement
14	whose body is one assignment is 3, `for i := 1 step 1 until 3 do ;` is 5,
15	`for i := 1, 2, 3 do ;` is 1) and says they "were checked against
16	`--max-steps` on ten small programs", which are not in the repository.
17	
18	**Implemented:** the four examples are written as made-up probe programs
19	(`qualification/programs/x08-*.alg`), and the qualification checks that the
20	harness's stage-step counts differ from a base probe by exactly 3, 3, 5 and
21	1. The ten programs themselves were not available.
22	
23	## A2. A per-stage budget, when the step limit is fixed at process start
24	
25	`PROTOCOL.md` gives each stage (and each spawned computation) its own budget
26	of 10⁶ steps, and the systems file says an ALGOL 60 program that reads each
27	stage as it arrives "counts as the same computation". The interpreter's only
28	step mechanism, `--max-steps N`, is set when the process starts, counts from
29	the start, and reports the count only when it stops the program. One
30	process cannot give stage 1 a budget of 10⁶ and stage 2 a budget of
31	R(1) + 10⁶.
32	
33	**Implemented** (report, x1): each stage, and each spawned computation, is
34	run in a **fresh interpreter process** that receives the earlier stages'
35	messages exactly as they first arrived (each after the previous `[end]`),
36	with `--max-steps R(k−1) + budget`, R(k−1) measured by bisection. The record
37	says `posed.how = "incremental"`, `replayed = []`, no restart cost, budget
38	10⁶: from the program's side the computation receiving stage k holds stages
39	1..k−1, received one by one, and its budget for stage k is exactly 10⁶. The
40	harness relies on the interpreter being deterministic, checks that the
41	re-created stages' output is byte-identical to their recorded output (else a
42	harness fault), does not repeat their output in `stdout`, and does not append
43	their emits to the effects log again. Every such attempt is **marked
44	explicitly**: its notes begin with `recreated_for_budget: true; …;
45	prefix_steps: R(k−1); prefix_commit_stages_carried_out_again: […]` (a note in
46	fixed form, since `record.schema.json` has no field for it and the common
47	schema is not changed here; a field `posed.recreated_for_budget` with
48	`steps.prefix_steps` would be the natural amendment). The prefix's steps are
49	recorded there and not charged to the stage. Listed as confound 1. *Why:* the
50	alternative readings were worse: charging an incremental program a restart
51	cost it does not have (calling every stage *reposed*), or one live process
52	whose stage budgets cannot be enforced. x1sim has no budget, so there it is
53	one live process.
54	
55	**Open:** at a commit stage inside the re-created prefix, the program
56	carries out the commit again (deterministically, its output checked to be
57	identical, so v is the same). `PROTOCOL.md` says a reposed run must not "ask
58	the system to select again"; this is not a reposed run, but the classifiers
59	may wish to know it, and it is recorded in the attempt's notes.
60	
61	## A3. spawn, and sharing unknowns (P09, P16b)
62	
63	ALGOL 60 has no separate computations, no concurrency and no unknowns.
64	
65	**Implemented:**
66	- *P09a, P09b*: a spawned computation is a part of the one program, started
67	  by the message `4 k c`, that runs to its end (or budget, or error) before
68	  the next is spawned, in the instance's `spawn_order`: `side_by_side:
69	  false`. They share the program's variables (the "one database"). In report
70	  and x1 each has its own budget (A2). If one ends the process (budget,
71	  error, timeout), there is no instance left to start the next in; the next
72	  is recorded as not started (`execution_state.determined: false`, no
73	  states, the reason in `basis`), not run in a separate instance.
74	- *P16b*: ALGOL 60 configurations do **not** allow separate computations to
75	  share unknowns (they have no unknowns), so stage 1 is posed to `main` as
76	  one conjunction (`1 1`), the `spawn_fallback`, with its `fallback_queries`.
77	  This is the harness's statement for all three configurations, made before
78	  any program is run, as the common Q4 asks.
79	
80	## A4. After budget, error or timeout, the replay repeats the stop
81	
82	An incremental ALGOL 60 program cannot continue past `--max-steps` or an
83	error (the process ends), so stage k+1 is reposed (`PROTOCOL.md`). The
84	program is deterministic, so the replay of stage k ends the same way, and
85	stage k+1 is never reached; every later stage is then recorded as *budget*,
86	*error* or *timeout* during the replay (the attempt's notes say which stage
87	of the replay stopped). After a final timeout each later stage again takes
88	the full limit and its rerun.
89	
90	**Implemented:** exactly that; the harness does not skip, shorten or work
91	around those stages (`harnesses/README.md` section 3: `run` never decides
92	from a result to skip a stage).
93	
94	## A5. Restart cost: never in-run
95	
96	The default method (Q6) reads the step count "at the moment stage k is first
97	posed". The interpreter cannot report its count at a moment of the harness's
98	choosing.
99	
100	**Implemented:** `restart_cost_method: "separate-run"` always: stages 1..k−1
101	alone (their messages written at once, then the input closed), the least
102	`--max-steps` at which the interpreter does not stop, found by bisection.
103	
104	## A6. Replayed stages' budgets in one process
105	
106	Q6 says each replayed stage has, during the replay, the budget it had when
107	first posed. In one process a single limit bounds the whole run.
108	
109	**Implemented:** the bisection for the restart cost searches up to the sum
110	of the replayed stages' budgets; the replay as a whole therefore has that sum,
111	not each stage its own. Where the replay does not end within the sum (it
112	replays a stage that ran out of budget, A4), the sum is recorded as
113	`restart_cost`, with a `restart_cost_source` saying the replay was not
114	measured to its end, and the run's limit is that plus the budget (so that
115	`budget = restart_cost + 10⁶`, as `validate.py` requires). A replayed stage
116	can therefore get more than its own budget in a reposed run; for a stage
117	that does not terminate that changes nothing but the step count at which it
118	is stopped.
119	
120	## A7. Store at the stage boundary
121	
122	The measurement build reports its quantities once, at the end of the
123	process, after the interpreter has returned and dropped every frame and
124	array, so the live quantities' "end" is 0, not their value at the stage
125	boundary.
126	
127	**Implemented:** live quantities (`frames`, `slots`, `arrays`,
128	`array_elements`, `names`, `call_depth`) have `boundary: null`; their peak
129	over the process (stages 1..k, as re-created) is the stage's `exact` peak
130	only where it exceeds the peak at the end of stage k−1 (from the previous
131	stage's storage run), else `null`. Totals are read at the boundary (the
132	process ends there). Confound 6.
133	
134	## A8. What a stage stopped by budget, error or timeout can observe
135	
136	`observe()` is to read state "including at the moment a budget runs out".
137	An ALGOL 60 program cannot print anything at that moment; the interpreter
138	stops it.
139	
140	**Implemented:** observe records what the program printed in the stage
141	before the stop (often nothing). The process is gone; nothing more can be
142	read.
143	
144	## A9. Steps in behaviour mode
145	
146	**Implemented:** in behaviour mode the harness measures R(k) only where a
147	later stage's budget needs it, and records it (Q17: incidental). The last
148	stage's steps, and those of a reposed program, are left null in behaviour
149	mode, with a note; the cost run gives them.
150	
151	## A10. `ended_by` for printed answers
152	
153	The program prints all it computes; there is no mechanism to ask for more.
154	
155	**Implemented:** `no-enumeration` when the stage ended with no more than cap
156	answers; `cap` when it printed more than cap (the first cap are collected,
157	the rest stay in `stdout` and `print`); `budget`, `error`, `timeout` when the
158	stage ended so.
159	
160	## A11. Constants and parameters on one input, without anticipation
161	
162	The interpreter has one input stream, and the contract wants constants read
163	"from a constants file the harness passes", the parameters n, order, answer
164	mode passed by the harness, and stages posed by the harness; and no stage's
165	information may reach the program before the stage is posed (`PROTOCOL.md`,
166	"Writing a program", rule 5).
167	
168	**Implemented** (revised before merge, at the coordinator's request): every
169	line of the constants file is tagged with the stage that first uses it
170	(`k: values…`). Standard input carries one line of instance parameters
171	(`n a m c1 … cm`), and then messages; each message that poses or replays
172	stage k (`1 k`, `2 k`, `3 k` + v, `4 k c`) is followed by stage k's lines, in
173	file order, with the tag removed. So no stage's constants are on the input
174	before that stage is posed, structurally, and a reposed run carries each
175	replayed stage's constants with its replay. The harness reads only the
176	tags, never the values. The verifier still substitutes only the constants
177	file (`ALGOL60_CONSTANTS`), which must keep the tags. String-valued
178	parameters (`order`, `spawn_order`) are passed as integer codes by their
179	first appearance in `stages.json` (README, 2.2). The qualification (F1)
180	traces every write to the system's input and checks it. Earlier version:
181	the whole file was sent before stage 1; the program's discipline alone kept
182	it from anticipating.
183	
184	## A12. The image's name
185	
186	The brief names the image `cp-agent-systems:spec-1.0`; `harnesses/README.md`
187	names `cp-systems:spec-1.0`. The harness ran in the former. It cannot read
188	the image digest from inside; `system_build.image` is taken from
189	`HARNESS_IMAGE` when the launcher passes it, else null.
190	
191	## A13. The X1 compiler as `check`
192	
193	`x1algc` compiles without running anything, but it accepts some programs
194	that are wrong (it accepted `k := 1 +;`, which x1sim then stopped at run
195	time with "Cannot pop empty stack"), and it writes its error report on
196	standard output, where the object code goes.
197	
198	**Implemented:** `check x1sim` runs only `x1algc` on a copy in a temporary
199	directory, discards the object code, prints the compiler's report on
200	failure, and says that the X1 compiler detects fewer errors than `algol60
201	--check`. An author may also check the X1-form program in x1.
202	
203	## A14. Input and output in x1
204	
205	`algol60 --x1` provides both the X1 system's procedures (`read`, `print`,
206	`PRINTTEXT`, …) and the Modified Report's (`ininteger`, `outstring`, …),
207	which the X1 did not have; the systems file lists only the IFIP procedures,
208	as external mechanisms of *report*.
209	
210	**Implemented:** the harness accepts either in x1, since it only reads
211	text. Which procedures count as core or external in x1 is for the
212	classifiers; the README recommends the X1 form, which also runs in x1sim.
213	
214	## A15. Exit status of an incremental attempt
215	
216	After the stage under test the harness closes the input, and the program's
217	next read ends the process with the interpreter's error (exit status 1).
218	
219	**Implemented:** `exit` records that status verbatim; the stage's execution
220	state is decided by its `[end]`, not by the exit status, and a note says so.
221	In x1sim the live process continues, so `exit` is null until the last stage,
222	and its final status is in the record's notes.
223	
224	## A16. A program that ends its own computation
225	
226	An incremental program that terminates (instead of reading its next
227	message) leaves no computation for the next stage.
228	
229	**Implemented:** the next stage is reposed, with `reason: "configuration"`
230	and a stage note saying the process had ended.
231	
232	## A17. Replaying a spawning stage
233	
234	`PROTOCOL.md` reposes every stage 1..k. No stage after a spawning stage
235	exists in `stages.json` except in P16b, whose spawning stage ALGOL 60 poses
236	by its fallback (A3).
237	
238	**Implemented:** replaying a spawning stage is not implemented; the harness
239	would record a harness fault if a stages file needed it.
240
